text: The seven values the sources leave open are read as follows and are written in the story as placeholders, never as guesses: the P5 generated-document request carries the case, the source GENERATED, the template code and version and the notice ID and answers with the document ID and the case; the document type and source a letter copy takes are read from the P5 document type list and the P6 source value GENERATED; no notice parameter is created and the parameters read stays wired and unconfigured; the P1 party and contact-point field IDs come from the P1 published contract; the NoticeGenerated payload carries notice ID, case ID, document ID, notice type, template code, template version and generation time; the hub-refusal message is MSG-GEN-006 naming the document hub; and the notice panel is described without an identifier
why: The sources fix the path, the owner, the event name and the field IDs of the notice and template tables, but not the payloads, the document type of a letter copy, the parameter names, the P1 field IDs, the full event schema or the screen identifier, and inventing any of them would put a business value into the build
read: ownership.json api row POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1, T3.2 and Appendix T-A; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 20 and 42; RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG sections 3 and 12.4
confirm: Solution architect confirms the P5 generated-document request and answer, the document type of a letter copy, the notice parameters and the event payload
impact: The client, the event schema and the message set are built against the published P5 document and the field IDs, and each placeholder is closed by one contract revision rather than by a code change

text: The story builds against the platform release train and the published P3 and P5 documents rather than against the nine DP-added contracts by name (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON), while the metadata table keeps the plan's Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E1032-CON and Ready to start Day 1
why: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 attaches those contracts to the patterns the story claims, but the plan's row for the story omits them and the plan is fixed for this run
read: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19; WP B-P6-05 story line for RWB-P6-E1032-APP
confirm: Release manager confirms the platform release train and the P3 and P5 contract dates for wave 1
impact: No build block on Day 1: the story compiles against the P5 fake and the platform libraries, and the dependency map understates the graph until the rows are added

text: The letter copy is handed to the document hub by the GenerateLetterCopy activity of NoticeDispatchWorkflow through the P5 generated-document operation, with source GENERATED and the case, the template code and version and the notice ID; the hub creates and owns the intake item, the match and the attach, and rwb-comms writes no document, document_intake or match row and serves no review decision
why: The integration story of the key asserts that the letter copy becomes an intake item, and no source states how a generated document becomes one; the architecture puts the generation on the call edge from rwb-comms to rwb-document, so the call is the only mechanism a source supports
read: RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG sections 2, 3 and 12.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 17 and 41; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.7; ownership.json (document, document_intake and document_type to P5)
confirm: Solution architect and the P5 owner confirm that the hub creates the intake item from the generated document and that the request needs no field this story does not send
impact: The handoff is one call with a 2 s budget and the item is P5's; a later decision to publish the item to rwb-comms changes the contract and not the notice row

text: No notice parameter is named or created by this story: the parameters read of DP-06 stays wired against the P3 parameters contract and answers nothing for this module until a register names a value, and the template code, the language, the product group, the notice type and the merge codes are read from the template and catalog rows and the P3 value lists instead
why: DP-06 is in the pattern set and the rule that no value a business person may change is written in code applies, but the P6 FSD and TSD declare no notice parameter at all
read: FSD P6 Communications v3 (parameter references belong to payment matching only); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and T3.2; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06 and section R3 default rulings
confirm: Business analyst confirms that the communications module has no parameter, or names the ones it has
impact: No business value reaches code: the values the copy merges are template, catalog and reference rows, and a parameter added later is a row and a read, not a release

text: The seventeen legacy test case IDs are carried on this story with their legacy fixtures, but the access case TC-E1-032-16 proves the notice-read refusal of rwb-comms and the Principle 5 case TC-E1-032-17 proves the decision-record failure on the letter-copy handoff, while the attach proof of the other fifteen stays with RWB-P5-E1032-APP; the story owns no legacy acceptance criterion
why: The WP keeps the seventeen legacy cases on this story and the integration story fixes that the legacy attach criteria belong to the P5 slice and the access and resilience criteria to the sibling APP stories, so the cases cannot be carried with their legacy subject
read: Legacy story RWB-E1-032 section 7 and section 16; RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 2 and section 19; WP B-P6-05 tcs_legacy list and acs []
confirm: Test lead confirms the carried cases and the coverage note in the test case register
impact: Every legacy case ID stays visible and traceable to a criterion of this story or of the P5 slice; the sentence in section 16 tells a reader which side of the split a case now proves

text: rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 keeps the consumer set of the event catalogue row, rwb-decision, and the document hub learns of the letter copy from the call and not from the event; the payload carries IDs and facts only, and a hub consumer would be a catalogue change
why: The event catalogue names rwb-decision as the only consumer and the architecture puts the letter generation on the call edge to rwb-document, while the integration story treats the copy that becomes an intake item as the evidence of the chain
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 42 row 13; RWB-ITG-E1032-ITG section 12.4
confirm: Solution architect confirms the mechanism once for the hub and the ledger
impact: One publisher, one consumer and one call; a second consumer is a catalogue and AsyncAPI change with a compatibility check, not a silent subscription

text: The FSD P6 Communications v3 and the TSD P6 Communications v2 are used as the reviewed baseline of this story, which stays at status Draft (realignment v1) until they are approved; no field, table, operation or rule used here is read as provisional
why: Both module documents are at status In review in the source set and the realignment run does not wait for approval, so the story records the assumption instead of stopping
read: FSD P6 Communications v3 document control; TSD P6 Communications v2 document control
confirm: Business analyst confirms the approved version of the two module documents
impact: Documentation only: the build is not blocked, and a change in the approved text arrives as a change request against a named version

text: The rescan notice is produced from one Approved and current version of a template row of schema rwb_comms whose body is the legacy MSG-P5-018 text with the merge codes {page}, {document} and {case}, whose language follows the language of the case in LOV-LANG, and whose channel is the ACE notification path. The template code, version, language, channel and body are carried as the placeholder of the gap until the template catalog story publishes the row, and this story reads the row and writes no template value of its own.
why: The legacy places the template in the ACE notification path under the name recovery templates and gives no code, version or channel, and the story cannot render or test the message without one named template.
read: RWB-E1-049 sections 3, 13 and 14 (MSG-P5-018); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (template, DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-069) and T3.2 (LOV-LANG, LOV-CHANNEL).
confirm: Business analyst P6 with the Legal counsel role and the template catalog owner, in the baseline review of the notice template.
impact: If the template stays in the notification path, one adapter call replaces the template read and no criterion changes; the message text and the hold reason stay as written.

text: The trigger is one event named rwb.document.OcrRescanRequested.v1 on topic rwb.document.events.v1, produced by P5 rwb-document in the same transaction as the intake item state change, with the element list intakeItemId, documentId, caseId (absent when no case), rescanPages, quality, languages and occurredAt; the name and the list are proposed because no source gives them, and the story builds against the proposed envelope and its fake until P5 publishes it in RWB-P5-E1049-CON.
why: The legacy notification is in-process and the event catalogue of Architecture v5 has no rescan event for the document service, so a decoupled notice has no named trigger.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17, 42 and 43; RWB-E1-049 sections 4 and 12; RWB-ITG-E1049-ITG section 12.4.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-document owner, in the baseline review of RWB-P5-E1049-CON and in the event catalogue next version.
impact: A different name or element list changes the listener, the fake and one consumed row; no table, workflow or published event of rwb-comms changes.

text: The six platform contract dependencies and the two rwb-case contract dependencies that the DP table adds are treated as the build and contract dependencies of this story in sections 3 and 13, together with the rwb-case case read, while the metadata keeps the empty build list and the single contract row of the plan; the story is therefore Day 1 against published contracts and fakes, and the correction of the plan is raised as a gap.
why: The story cannot build the outbox, the workflow, the migration, the reference reads or the case read without those contracts, and the plan's lists do not carry them although the pattern table the story applies does.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 (DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-15, DP-19) and section R5.7 rule 8; _work/msr/wp/B-P6-05.md story line RWB-P6-E1049-APP.
applied_in: RWB-P6-E1049-APP sections 3 and 13; the metadata table as the plan states it
confirm: Solution architect and the dependency map owner, when the dependency map next version is produced.
impact: If the plan is corrected the metadata rows change and nothing else; the Day-1 position and the lane do not change.

text: The notice row of the rescan notice carries a notice_type read from LOV-NOTICE, and because the list has no value for an operational message to the case owner the field is carried as the placeholder until the business owner publishes one value; the notice is identified meanwhile by its template reference, its message text and its case and document references, and none of the four customer values is written on the row.
why: The field is mandatory on the notice row and every value of the list describes a customer notice, so writing one of them would misstate the row.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-018) and T3.2 (LOV-NOTICE); RWB-E1-049 section 10 and section 14.
confirm: Business owner with the business analyst P6, in the reference-data review that publishes the list value.
impact: Publishing the value adds one reference row and one assertion and changes no criterion, because the criteria assert the message, the case, the document and the dispatch facts.

text: The {document} token of MSG-P5-018 is filled from the document read of rwb-document with the display reference that contract returns, and with the document identifier where the contract returns none, so the same document always reads the same in the message and the text stays byte-identical for one document.
why: MSG-P5-018 names the document in the message and no source says which reference form the token carries, while the message has to read the same in a test, in a log excerpt and in a notice read months later.
read: RWB-E1-049 section 14 (MSG-P5-018); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-017); RWB-ITG-E1049-ITG section 12.2 (the document read).
confirm: Business analyst P6 with the rwb-document owner, in the baseline of the message text.
impact: A different reference form changes one merge step and the expected string of AC1; no contract, table or event changes.

text: The only sender is the ACE common notification path, called under the service identity of rwb-comms with the recipient reference of the case owner, the channel from the template, the template reference and language, the case reference and the merged message, and answered with an accepted external reference and one result code; the service calls NSS or LINE OA directly in no case, so the story declares no external dependency and its shape is the placeholder of the gap until the path owner publishes it.
why: Architecture v5 gives the notification path to ACE Common as the OUT call of rwb-comms and TSD P6 routes NSS and LINE through it, while no source gives a request or result shape and DP-16 is not among the patterns of the key.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (OUT: REST ACE Common, notification path, SMS and LINE); TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.1 (INT-17, INT-18) and T5.2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.3.4.3.
confirm: ACE notification path owner with the solution architect, before the wave 1 SIT entry.
impact: A different shape changes the adapter, the stub and the assertions of AC1 and AC6; the provided read, the events and the tables do not change.

text: The dispatch retries the send once under the retry policy of the workflow kit and the attempt count is written on the notice row, once per attempt; the attempt limit, the interval and the exception rule beyond that single retry follow the platform resilience rules R-UNI-33 and R-UNI-34 and are carried as the placeholder of the gap rather than fixed here, and no Schedule of rwb-comms is registered for the retry.
why: The criterion asserts one retry and the module extract names a retry limit of five with an exception queue for a message, so a value has to be fixed for the test while the wider limit is not given for a notice.
read: RWB-E1-049 BR5 (R-UNI-33); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.3.4.3 AC-EXC-P6-003-03; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-11 outbox sender, every service, every minute).
confirm: Platform workflow owner with the DevOps lead, before the alert of the attempt limit is registered.
impact: A different limit or interval changes a values file and one test of AC6; the notice row, the events and the read do not change.

text: The feature flag of the capability is read through the platform feature-flag library, which owns flags under the default ruling, and off means the listener drops the rescan event and writes no notice; the flag name follows the service naming and is the placeholder of the gap, so no name is fixed in code or in a test.
why: The default ruling gives feature flags to the platform library and the legacy story switches the OCR step with a flag of the document service, while no source names a flag of the notice.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R3 (feature flags, platform library); RWB-E1-049 section 3 (feature flag rwb.dochub.ocr) and section 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20.
confirm: Platform library owner with the DevOps lead, when the flag is registered in the environment.
impact: A flag name is a values-file entry; a change of owner would add one library client and one consumed row.

text: The default ruling that parameters and reference data belong to rwb-case is accepted: this story reads no parameter, the four OCR values stay rows of the document hub parameter table of P5 rwb-document, and the two values a business person may change in this capability, the template reference and its channel, are rows of the service's own template table and not parameters, so no parameter is duplicated in rw_comms.
why: DP-06 is among the patterns of the key and the legacy story reads OCR_MIN_QUALITY from a parameter table, so the ruling has to be stated for the slice even though no parameter is read in it.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R3 (parameters and reference data, E1-042 and E1-043, to P3) and section R5.5 DP-06; RWB-E1-049 sections 3 and 11 (DF-REF-246 document_hub_parameter).
applied_in: RWB-P6-E1049-APP sections 3, 11 and 13; the threshold stays with RWB-P5-E1049-APP
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-case and rwb-document owners, in the baseline review of the OCR parameters.
impact: If a value must become a parameter it is added to the rwb-case contract and read there; no table of rw_comms changes its shape.

text: The default ruling that reference data belongs to rwb-case is accepted: LOV-NOTICE, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-LANG and LOV-SENT-TYPE are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case on every rendering and on the read of the notice, the service holds no local copy and no list value is written in code, and a list that does not answer holds the notice rather than sending it with a guessed value.
why: DP-07 is among the patterns of the key, TSD P6 T6.1 declares reference lists the service does not own, and the notice cannot be rendered without the language and channel lists.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R3 (reference data, E1-043, to P3) and section R5.5 DP-07; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.3.1.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-case owner, in the reference-data baseline review.
impact: If a list stays local, one copy table and one migration step are added; the read and the criteria do not change.

text: The default ruling that the interaction ledger belongs to rwb-source-data is accepted and this notice writes no ledger row: the notice row carries the dispatch facts of the message, the two events carry IDs and facts, and no rw_source_data table is read or written from rw_comms.
why: The legacy notification writes an interaction in the shared recovery schema, DP-18 gives the ledger to rwb-source-data and DP-18 adds no dependency to this key, so a ledger write here would need a contract this story does not have.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R3 (interaction ledger, P1) and section R5.5 DP-18; Ownership Map (interaction owner P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner and the data steward.
impact: If a ledger row is required, one consumed row, one fake and one contract dependency are added; the notice table and the read do not change.

text: The area and the right of the notice read are declared on the operation and enforced at gateway-bff, this story makes no rwb-access call because DP-08 is not among its patterns, and a request that reaches the service without the declared right is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 without returning the notice; the scope of a case is decided on the case read the story already makes.
why: TSD P6 declares a Litigation right on the notice read and no rwb-access story is a build or contract dependency of this key, so the enforcement point has to be stated for the access case to have a subject.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.2 (API-P6-002, Litigation right R, scope applied); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-08 and DP-19; Ownership Map api row GET /notices/{noticeId}.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access owner and the gateway-bff owner, in the baseline review of RWB-P6-E1049-CON.
impact: If a service-side authorise call is required, DP-08 and RWB-P4-E1037-CON are added with one client call and one fake; the refusal and its message stay as written.

text: The Notice answer of GET /notices/{noticeId} carries id, caseId, caseNo, documentId, templateId, templateCode, templateVersion, language, noticeType, message, state, holdReason, sentDate, deliveryStatus and dispatchAttempts in camelCase from the field names of the notice table, and the state values of a notification-path dispatch are Generated, Dispatched and Held with Sent, Delivered and Unserved kept for the letter path of other stories; the full list is the placeholder of the gap until the contract baseline is published.
why: The module extract names the resource and the table fields only, and the app story, its component tests and the integration suite cannot read or assert the notice without one fixed answer.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 (DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-034) and T-A.2 (API-P6-002); FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.1.4.2 and AC-EXC-P6-001-02.
confirm: Solution architect with the consumers of the notice answer, in the baseline review of the notice contract.
impact: An added or renamed optional property is an additive change of major version 1; a state value added later is a reference row and one assertion.

text: The cost alert is not case-bound, so rwb-comms serves it on the published message operation POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/messages with the alert reference supplied by P10 in the path position of the case identifier, makes no case lookup and reads no recovery_case row, stores the notice with that reference in notice.case_id, and returns it on GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId} so a reader can tie the notice to the alert.
why: The legacy story sends MSG-P10-004 through a notification interface that has no case, while the P6 message operation of the module specification is case-bound and requires the Case record right; the integration story states that the alert is not case-bound and is proved at the P6 boundary, and no source names a non-case notification operation.
read: RWB-E1-063 sections 4 step 5, 5 X5, 7 AC2 and AC7 and 12; Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P6-008; Arch v5 slides 17, 20 and 41; RWB-ITG-E1063-ITG section 7 AC2, BR7 and section 12.2; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-11 and DP-13.
applied_in: Story sections 2, 3, 4 steps 2 to 9, 5 X9, 7 AC1, 11 and 12.1
confirm: P6 comms owner and P10 agent owner
impact: The message text, the two recipient roles and the one-notice rule stay exactly as the legacy story fixes them; only the carrier of a case-less notification changes, and no case value is read or invented.

text: P10 rwb-agent announces a cost alert on rwb.agent.events.v1 with a proposed event named rwb.agent.AgentAlertRaised.v1 that carries the alert reference and the facts that identify the alert, and rwb-comms treats the event as a trigger only: it reads the alert facts back through GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics before it writes a notice, so no amount, cap or role is taken from the event body.
why: The legacy story raises the alert and calls the notification interface in one step and publishes no event, and the event catalogue of Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 carries AgentRunCompleted as the only P10 event, so no source names the alert event.
read: RWB-E1-063 sections 4 step 5, 5 X5 and 12 (events published: none); Arch v5 slides 16 (P10 OUT: rwb.agent.events.v1 carries AgentRunCompleted), 42 and 43 (event catalogues) and 41 (service catalogue); Template and Rules v1 section R4 (event naming rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1) and section R5.5 DP-09; RWB-ITG-E1063-ITG section 12.2 and ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1063-5.
applied_in: Story sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 3, 5 X8, 7 AC1 and AC5, 11, 12.2 and 12.4
confirm: P10 agent owner
impact: A redelivered or stale event cannot put a wrong amount in a notice, because every value is read from the contract; the event name is a proposal until P10 publishes its AsyncAPI document.

text: The eight dependency rows that DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 add are treated as the wave-0 service template baseline: the five platform contracts H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, and the gateway route H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, are already held by every wave-1 service, and the two P3 reads C RWB-P3-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON are answered by their contract fakes until those contracts are published, so neither the Day-1 start nor the Done of this story is blocked.
why: The plan line of this story carries no build dependency and one contract dependency only, while the pattern set includes six decoupling patterns whose DP table rows add eight dependencies, and section R5.7 makes an APP story build against CON stories and their fakes.
read: _work/msr/wp/B-P6-05.md story line RWB-P6-E1063-APP; Template and Rules v1 sections R5.4, R5.5 (DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19) and R5.7; Arch v5 slides 20 and 44.
confirm: Platform owner, P3 case owner and delivery lead
impact: The story starts on Day 1 in lane L-P6-I; the dependency map is incomplete until the eight rows are added, and the two P3 reads run against their fakes in the meantime.

text: The agent cost alert template of the P6 template set keeps the MSG-P10-004 text unchanged and is seeded in the template catalog with a configured code, language, channel and version; the template code, the channel and the notice type are versioned parameter or reference rows read through the P3 parameters and reference-data contracts; the retry window and the attempt limit are platform outbox configuration; the role holders of RW-COE and RW-RISK are resolved from the role model and not from a list in this service; and the guard right of the cost-alert notice read is declared at gateway-bff.
why: The legacy story names the template by its plain description only, the module specification's notice-type list has no entry for an agent cost alert, and no source read here gives the channel, the retry window, the holder list or the guard right; section R5.5 DP-06 and DP-07 and the platform rule on feature flags fix where the configurable values live.
read: RWB-E1-063 sections 3, 4 step 5, 5 X5, 7 AC2 and AC7, 13 (Notification template agent cost alert for MSG-P10-004 in the P6 template set) and 14; FSD P6 A2.3 to A2.6 (MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-P6-003, retry limit 5, R-UNI-34); TSD P6 T3.1, T3.2 LOV-CHANNEL and LOV-NOTICE, and T-A.2 API-P6-002 and API-P6-008; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-06, DP-07 and section R3 default rulings (parameters and reference data to P3); Arch v5 slide 20 (the notification path through ACE Common).
applied_in: Story sections 3, 5 X6, 7 AC1, 11, 12.1, 12.8, 13 configuration and 14
confirm: P6 comms owner and platform notification path owner
impact: The message text and the two recipient roles stay the legacy ones; the configured code, channel and window are visible in one place each and no business value is written in code.

text: There is no data lake and no dashboard copy in the rwb-comms slice: the daily agent measures are a P9 rwb-reporting read model built from rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 and the P10 daily step, the alert, the cap and the alert role are P10 data, and the Power BI page Agent monitor v1 is not built anywhere; rwb-comms builds only the cost-alert notification and recomputes no measure.
why: Arch v5 slide 37 removes the data lake and the Power BI feed and replaces them with reports from rwb-reporting; DP-17 records it as a decoupling with no dependency added; the legacy agent_run_daily table and the Power BI page therefore have no target, and no source names a dashboard deliverable that stays in P6.
read: RWB-E1-063 sections 2, 3, 4, 7 AC1, AC3 and AC4, 12 and 15; Arch v5 slide 37 and slide 41 (P9 rwb-reporting owns the measures and the steering dashboard, P6 rwb-comms owns the notices); Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17 and section R6 (RWB-E1-014 retired); RWB-ITG-E1063-ITG section 7 AC8 and section 19.
applied_in: Story sections 2, 3, 4 step 11, 8 BR6 and BR7, 11, 12.7, 13 and 15
confirm: Architecture owner, P9 reporting owner and P6 comms owner

text: REQ-DRI-009 is read as the reporting requirement it describes and not as a requirement on rwb-comms: the daily agent measures are available from the P9 rwb-reporting read model with the row counts matched against the P10 source, and the notification of a cost breach is the only part of the legacy story that remains with rwb-comms. The requirement identifier and its owner are unchanged and no date is changed.
why: The requirement wording still names a daily copy to the data lake, which Arch v5 slide 37 and DP-17 remove, and section R3 puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the story masters and above the BRD wording that the story copies.
read: Business Requirements Program v4 section 5.7 row REQ-DRI-009; Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 row REQ-DRI-009; Arch v5 slide 37; Template and Rules v1 sections R3, R5.5 DP-17 and R6; RWB-ITG-E1063-ITG sections 7 AC8 and AC9 and 18.
confirm: Data steward and data product owner
impact: The traceability row of REQ-DRI-009 stays in the story and points at the P10 alert contract and the two published notice events; the requirement text is corrected in the next BRD version, and the release date 30 November 2026 is copied unchanged and stays tentative.

text: The rule package rwb-comms evaluates is read as reference data through the reference-data contract of rwb-case, one row per package a service is assigned, and until that map is published the story is built and tested on the legacy ALLOCATION fixtures marked as synthetic test data: package ALLOCATION with versions ALLOC-2026.11 (24 rows, in force), ALLOC-2026.12 (26 rows), ALLOC-2026.13 and ALLOC-2026.17, package TRANSFER with TRF-2026.11, the rows ALLOC-014, ALLOC-015, ALLOC-031, ALLOC-032, ALLOC-040, ALLOC-041 and ALLOC-999, the scenarios TA-07 and TA-19, and the queues MTG-BKK-CO, MTG-UPC-CO, MTG-CEN-CO and GEN-CO. No fixture value reaches production as a constant: the package code, the version labels and the queues are rows.
why: The integration story gives rwb-comms the local copy and the evaluation of the package it is assigned but no source names that package, and the ownership map assigns no rule package to P6; without a package the model fetch, the local copy and the scenario set cannot be built or tested. Every value used is copied from the legacy story and the two design decks, so nothing is invented.

text: The model fetch is GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{versionLabel} on the rwb-decision base, one hop with a 2 s client budget, a breaker and one GET retry, and its answer carries the generated DRL of the version, its SHA-256 checksum, its version state and its valid from date; an unknown label answers 404, a version that cannot be loaded answers 409, an empty model answers 422 and a failure answers 503. The story builds against a WireMock fake of that shape until RWB-P7-E1073-APP publishes the operation.
why: Arch v5 slides 14 and 27 and the Temporal and Drools design slide 15 name only the path family GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}; no source gives the path segments, the media type, the placement of the checksum or how the local load learns the version state and the valid from date, and the operation is in neither the Ownership Map nor API Specification v4. A local load cannot verify a checksum or refuse a version that is not APPROVED without those four values.

text: The local evaluated copy is one row per package version in schema rwb_comms, keyed on the package code and the version label, holding the version label, the SHA-256 checksum, the local state, the valid from date and the load time, and the copy in use is the single row in state verified; a restart reads that row and the KieBaseRegistry compiles the model again from the last good copy before it answers anything. The DB story of the service names the table and the columns.
why: The design says each service holds its own approved copy and keeps the last good model, but no source gives the table, the columns, the state values or where the copy survives a restart, and the Ownership Map has no local-copy table. The migration and the repository cannot be written without a shape.

text: rwb-comms consumes rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 from rwb.decision.events.v1, CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode keyed on caseId where a case is named and on the package code otherwise, deduped in processed_event, retried at 1 minute, 10 minutes and 1 hour and then sent to the .dlt topic; the payload carries the package code, the version label, the SHA-256 checksum and the valid from date and nothing else. The slide 43 consumer list is read as a subset of the slide 20 rule that every service refreshes its cache on the event.

text: The scenario set re-run locally is the Tests-tab scenario set stored with the package version, delivered in the model fetch answer or read with it as a list of scenario ID, facts, expected queue and expected outcome, at least rules.testcases.min (50) entries; the local run stores its result as the pass count and the failing scenario IDs on the local run record of the version, and a version whose scenario set is absent or shorter than the minimum is refused exactly as a failing scenario is.

text: One notice is produced per approval and per escalation level: the inbox dedupe of DP-09 and a unique key on the notice kind, the approval reference and the escalation level make a second notice impossible, and a repeated message request with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first notice with status 200.

impact: A replay or a duplicate request writes nothing and sends nothing; the approver is never told twice about one breach

text: A withdrawn template, or one with no Approved version current on the business date, holds the notice with hold reason TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN and raises MSG-P6-003 to the owner of the template; nothing is sent, and the item stays with the new approver because rwb-decision has already moved it.
why: FSD P6 v3 VR-P6-001-1 and MSG-P6-003 fix the hold and the message for a withdrawn template, and this story's item was moved by another service before the notice was rendered.
read: FSD P6 v3 A2.1.3.1 VR-P6-001-1, A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-P6-001-02 and A2.4.3.1 VR-P6-004-2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-04; legacy RWB-E2-013 section 13
confirm: The template owner confirms which role receives the MSG-P6-003 task for an approver notification template
impact: The notice is held and nothing is sent; the approval and the case are untouched, so the only loss is the telling, which is visible on the held notice

text: When the ACE notification path is unavailable the notice is kept with sent_at empty, MSG-GEN-006 naming the path is recorded, and the outbox retries; the retry that succeeds sends once and sets sent_at once, and a repeat of a message the path already accepted is refused by the path's own idempotency so no second send happens.
why: FSD P6 v3 AC-EXC-P6-003-03 retries an unavailable NSS send on a schedule and ends in the exception queue under R-UNI-34, and DP-09 makes the outbox the retry mechanism of the target; the retry limit and backoff are the platform's.
read: FSD P6 v3 A2.3.4.3 AC-EXC-P6-003-03 and A2.8 exception flow AC-EXC-P6-008-03; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20
confirm: Platform team states the outbox retry limit and backoff for a send in RWB-PLT-TE006-CON
impact: A path outage delays the telling and never duplicates it; the notice read shows the pending send while the retry runs
